headline: GlobalFoundries has agreed to make silicon interposers in New York for TSMC's AI chip packaging, in a deal reported at about $2 billion.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 6: the deal was announced on 8 Oct 2026; today's item is an analysis of it.
importance_line: It adds a US source for a scarce part of AI chip packaging, which matters to Nvidia, Apple and AMD as TSMC customers, but it covers only interposers, so packaging shortages remain.
summary: digitimes reports in an analysis that GlobalFoundries, a US contract chipmaker, has a multiyear agreement with TSMC to expand silicon interposer capacity (the layer that links AI processors to memory chips) at its Malta, New York, plant for TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging line. TradingKey adds that the deal, announced on 8 Oct 2026, is reported at about $2 billion over five years, with volume production ramping from the first half of 2028, and covers interposers only, not chip assembly and testing.
notes: digitimes text paywalled; deal figures from TradingKey, which cites media reports.
